This is an MCP-server/protocol-implementation guide for building Microsoft 365 Copilot Chat widgets (OpenAI Apps SDK / MCP Apps, mcpPlugin.json manifests, devtunnels, atk CLI provisioning, MCP Inspector tool-schema workflow) -- it is fundamentally an agent/backend engineering skill, not a design skill; the one design-adjacent requirement is 'use React + Fluent UI components' for widget rendering, which is a one-line dependency mandate, not design guidance. It is hard-wired to Microsoft 365 Copilot's specific proprietary infrastructure (mcpPlugin.json schema v2.4, m365.cloud.microsoft CORS origins, atk CLI, devtunnel service) and is unusable outside that ecosystem. Rubric: relevance 1 (only tangentially touches UI via a dependency mandate), quality 2 (detailed and actionable, but for MCP/protocol engineering not design), conformance 0 (requires Microsoft's specific private/proprietary M365 Copilot and Apps SDK services baked directly into the instructions -- 'Unusable outside its origin' per rubric), uniqueness 1. Total 4, and relevance 1 is below the vendor threshold. Not a design-relevant skill for this registry's scope.
rejectedSkills.securityNotes: SKILL.md read in full. No exfiltration or credential-harvesting instructions found; it does instruct the agent to run background OS processes (devtunnel, MCP server) unattended and to fully automate installs/auth without asking the user first ('FULL AUTOMATION... Never tell the user to run commands manually'), which is aggressive-automation guidance worth flagging to a human reviewer even though it targets the user's own local dev environment rather than a third party. This is a relevance-driven rejection, not primarily a security rejection, but the automation posture reinforces that this skill is out of scope for a design-focused registry.
